workflow.name: 🎯 Demo — Agent: Invoice OCR Pipeline
workflow.description: Built live by the workflow agent (Azure gpt-5.4): a linear Azure-OCR + cleanup pipeline.

steps: Open the chat-log link — the drawer replays the full agent conversation (prompt + every tool call).
Watch the agent read the catalog, then create the workflow and add nodes in dependency order.
Open the workflow link to inspect the built graph: upload → prepare → Azure OCR (submit/poll/extract) → cleanup → store.

parts.text: Build a new workflow named 'Demo — Invoice OCR Pipeline'. Goal: accept an uploaded document, prepare it, run Azure OCR on it (submit, then poll for the result, then extract the OCR result), then clean up the OCR text and store the OCR results. Check the activity and source catalogs first, then create the workflow, add the nodes in dependency order, connect them, and set the upload node as the entry point. Do NOT run it — no sample file is available. Stop when the graph is complete and tell me the final node chain.

Done — the workflow graph is complete and I did not run it.

Final node chain:
`upload1 (source.upload) → prepare1 (file.prepare) → submit1 (azureOcr.submit) → poll1 (azureOcr.poll) → extract1 (azureOcr.extract) → cleanup1 (ocr.cleanup) → store1 (ocr.storeResults)`

Notes:
- Workflow name: `Demo — Invoice OCR Pipeline`
- Entry point: `upload1`
- Azure OCR model parameter set on:
  - `poll1`: `modelId = "prebuilt-read"`
  - `extract1`: `modelId = "prebuilt-read"`

One caveat:
- `ocr.storeResults` typically needs a `documentId` input in addition to `ocrResult`.
- The graph is connected, and auto-wiring resolved the OCR result path, but there is no upstream node in this chain that clearly provides `documentId`, so storage may need one more source of document identity later if you want this workflow to execute successfully.

If you want, I can next add the missing document-id path in a follow-up edit.
